title: Software Engineering, B.S. (Behrend)
notes: PATTERN B -- no University Park equivalent exists at all (checked `ls Backend/degree_plans | sed -E 's/-[0-9]{4}\.json$//' | sort -u`: no SWENG-prefixed major existed before this file). Software Engineering, B.S. is Penn State Behrend's only undergraduate software engineering program in the whole PSU system, an ABET-accredited engineering major distinct from both UP's CMPSC and Behrend's own separate Computer Science, B.S. (Behrend) (CMPSCBH-2026.json). Since no UP major of this name exists, used a short sensible all-caps code (SWENG, matching the department's real course prefix) rather than a 'BH' suffix, per this session's instructions. Built from Behrend's own 2026-27 Suggested Academic Plan and 'Requirements for the Major' course table at Erie Campus (bulletins.psu.edu/undergraduate/colleges/behrend/software-engineering-bs/, fetched 2026-08-27) -- every required course and credit value below matches that page. Entrance-to-major requires CHEM 110, MATH 140, MATH 141, and PHYS 211 with a C or better and a 2.0 cumulative GPA (marked etm below). Technical electives (9cr, 3 slots): the bulletin's own School-Approved Electives page requires at least 2 Primary Technical Electives and at most 1 Secondary; modeled as 2 slots matched against the real Primary list (any 300/400-level EE, CMPEN, SWENG, or CMPSC-except-474/335 course, or GAME 450/480) and 1 slot matched against the real Secondary list (BME 402/406, SWENG 395/495, MIS 430/435/445/470, MGMT 409, PSYCH 444, ECON 481/485, MATH 455/456, ENTR 430, DIGIT 430). EE 210 (4cr) or EE 211 (3cr) is modeled at a fixed 4cr, an approximation of the bulletin's stated '3-4' range for this slot. Added minimal catalog entries this session for SWENG 311/411/421/431/452W/480/481 (catalogs/sweng_catalog.json) -- SWENG had no prior catalog in this app (also shared by CMPSCBH-2026.json's computing-elective/track-elective slots). REAL HIDDEN PREREQ GAPS found while verifying this plan actually simulates cleanly (same category CMPSC-2026.json's own notes already document for UP, and the same fix convention PREMED-2026.json/PHILBS-2026.json use for their own MATH-placement gaps): (1) this app's shared cmpsc_catalog.json gives CMPSC 121 a hard prereq of MATH 110 (not satisfied merely by concurrently taking the more advanced MATH 140), and gives CHEM 110 a hard prereq of MATH 22 -- both real courses this bulletin explicitly requires. Rather than fabricate a substitution, the real MATH chain is scheduled explicitly: MATH 21 (Semester 1, no prereq) -> MATH 22 (Semester 2, needs MATH 21) -> CHEM 110 and MATH 110 (Semester 3, both need MATH 22) -> CMPSC 121 (Semester 4, needs MATH 110). (2) CMPSC 431W and CMPSC 461 -- both real required SWENG courses -- have a shared-catalog hard prereq of CMPSC 221 (Object-Oriented Programming with Web-Based Applications), a course this bulletin's own required-course list never mentions; CMPSC 221 is added explicitly (Semester 6) purely to unlock those two required courses, the same 'add a real course purely to satisfy a downstream prereq' convention CMPSC-2026.json's own notes use for CMPSC 311/CMPSC 483W. (3) EE 210/211 both require PHYS 212 (a real prereq, not concurrent) -- the original suggested-plan pairing had them in the same term; moved EE 210/211 to the term after PHYS 212 completes. These fixes push the whole plan to 9 real terms (4.5 calendar years) instead of the bulletin's nominal 8 semesters -- registered with grad_years=5 in tests.py, the same override BMB/CHE/IID/MICRB/PREMED/DS/EE already use for their own real prereq-chain overflows. Total credits across all 9 semesters sum to 134 (126-127 real bulletin credits, plus 10cr of MATH 21/22/110 remediation the bulletin's suggested plan doesn't show because it assumes students test out of it, plus 3cr for the added CMPSC 221 prereq-unlock course).
